ID: `humanizer`.

## What it does

Reads the entire text and looks for repeated contrast formulas, conclusions that restate the point, generic emphasis, uniform rhythm and chat residue. Rewrites using the available information and voice, then checks that facts, quotations and degree of certainty are preserved. In files, edits only prose, leaving code, paths and metadata intact.

## When to use it

Use it for text with sound content that feels built from automated formulas. It suits documentation, articles and copy; editorial work does not certify whether the author is human or a model.

## How to use it

Ask for it by name, or invoke it with `/humanizer` in Claude Code or `$humanizer` in Codex. Provide the text, context and an optional voice sample. Specify terms and quotations to preserve. Request a natural, faithful revision without adding personal experiences, examples or data absent from the sources.

## What it delivers

- Revised prose
- Preserved information and voice
- Summary of changes when working on files

## Example

Rewrite this guide for clarity, preserving procedures and constraints. Cut passages that repeat the same idea and leave code examples intact.
